newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss prepare for possible 1988 Telecom float.
newsitem.headline: Swiss prepare for possible 1988 Telecom float.

text.p: The Swiss transportation and energy ministry is preparing for partial flotation of Telecom AG in the second half of 1998, but a final decision on the date for a stock market listing will not be taken before next year.
The ministry said in a statement the cabinet last week asked the ministry to start preparatory work for a listing so it was an option that Telecom could be listed in the second half of 1998.
"Definitive decisions about a partial privatisation will first be taken in 1998," the ministry said.
The Swiss government is planning to liberalise its postal and telecommunications market on January 1, 1998, in line with the European Union.
In December 1996 the lower house of parliament on approved a government proposal to split the postal and telecommunications authority into two separate units.
While telecommunications activities will be transformed into a joint stock company with the government holding a majority, the postal authority will remain a state-owned agency.
The upper house of parliament is expected to debate and approve the reform during this month's session.

However, at the same time the reform takes effect, decrees governing the two units must be in place, including such issues as the government's role and the operational makeup of the post and telecommunications units.
The ministry is therefore laying the groundwork for the government to take decisions on the strategic goals of Post and Telecom, its boards and the opening financial accounts.
J.P. Morgan has been chosen to advise the government on the financial issues involved in founding Telecom AG, while Credit Suisse First Boston, a unit of Credit Suisse, is advising Telecom.
The ministry said the government wants to determine these issues by September.
However, the government cannot make any decisions until the second half of this year because it has to wait at least 90 days before the deadline for holding a referendum about the reform expires.
The Swiss trade body representing five unions, encompassing 46,000 postal and Telecom workers, has said it is opposed to the reforms and the unions are considering a referendum.
